stewart_read: The rep hit a mismatch between satellite imagery and the customer's actual property and paused the whole flow on it instead of proceeding with the roof/garage info already given.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically deferring to get accurate imagery before quoting — but no bill, utility, or appointment time was captured in the meantime, so nothing was gained from continuing the call.
coaching_implication: Capture remaining verify items (bill, utility) while flagging imagery for the design team, instead of stopping the whole call on it.

quote: I can give you a callback once I have more updated imagery. Does that work for you? Fine. Yep.
stewart_read: No specific day or time is proposed for the callback — this is a soft, procedurally fragile close with no ownership of a concrete next step.
coaching_implication: Even when deferring for imagery, lock a specific callback day/time and confirm bill + utility before ending the call.

coaching_implication: Reflect back new-build details ('brand new garage, no shading — that's actually great for solar') to keep energy moving forward instead of using it as the reason to punt.

alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this not worth expanding given the call's early derailment into imagery issues.
coaching_implication: When the stated interest reason is unclear, ask a clarifying follow-up rather than moving straight to the next verify item — this is the emotional anchor for the whole pitch.

quote: Let me check with my design team. I'm not it might be, like, looking at older imagery then.
stewart_read: Rep abandons the standard verify sequence (bill, utility) to resolve a design-team question mid-call, effectively ending the call's productive work early.

coaching_implication: Separate the imagery/design-team issue from the qualification checklist; keep collecting bill and utility info while flagging imagery for later.
